thread.title: Morning Movers: Disney Jumps Despite Supersized Bid for Fox; Citigroup Rallies

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Morning Movers: Disney Jumps Despite Supersized Bid for Fox; Citigroup Rallies
text:
By Ben Levisohn June 20, 2018 9:24 a.m. ET The Dow Jones Industrial Average is bouncing back from yesterday's losses. In today's Morning Movers , we...
Illustration: Getty Images •...do the math on tariff impacts on both GDP and S&P 500 earnings;
•...explain why Walt Disney (DIS) is rising;
•...highlight an upgrade of Citigroup (C).
What's There to Worry About Again? The market's rallying today from its trade-related selloff in the absence of new negative headlines to scare investors.
S&P 500 futures have advanced 0.3%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have gained 110 points, or 0.5%, and is trying to break a six-day losing streak . Nasdaq Composite futures have risen 0.4%.
Maybe there's something to more relaxed view on trade , at least for now. A Deutsche Bank analysis this morning that an additional $200 billion in tariffs would reduce real GDP by 0.2 to 0.3 percentage, and that drag would translate into a 1 to 1.5% reduction in earnings growth. "In the context of 2018 EPS growth which is on track to hit [forecasts] of 23% and 2019 growth estimated in double-digits, a 1-1.5% drag is not particularly significant," writes Deutsche Bank's Torsten Sløk . "While the indirect effects of uncertainty and hit to business confidence are harder to gauge...corporates [could respond] by putting more of their cashflow towards share buybacks, the primary driver of equities in this cycle from a demand-supply perspective."
And tech could continue to benefit if trade with China continues to be an issue. DataTrek's Nicholas Colas notes that despite having the highest exposure to international trade, at 58%, tech been the best returning sector. What gives? Colas points to the fact that U.S. tech companies, aside from Apple (AAPL), have little exposure to China, and even Apple has mitigating factors."By virtue of China’s home grown tech giants (Tencent, Alibaba (BABA), Baidu (BIDU)) and the US’s own leaders (Apple, Alphabet (GOOGL), Facebook ( FB), etc), there is little overlap between the two countries and that’s proving to be a powerful positive for US large cap Tech stocks," he explains. "Yes, Apple has China exposure but Facebook and Google are both banned. And, of course, Apple’s largest manufacturing partner is China, which helps."
One more reason tech can keep on keeping on.
Morning Movers Earnings & News
General Electric (GE) is down 1.7% to $12.73 on news that Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA), up 2.9% to $66.48, will replace it in the Dow Jones Industrial Average .
Illustration: Bloomberg News Oracle (ORCL) is down 4.3% to $44.30 after reporting fourth-quarter earnings . The tech giant earned 99 cents a share on revenue of $11.26 billion, while analysts were looking for 94 cents on revenue of $11.17 billion. For the first quarter, it warned that foreign exchange had moved from a 3% tailwind to a 1% headwind, and it expects to earn between 67 cents and 69 cents a share, below the 71 cent per-share consensus.
Starbucks (SBUX) is down 3.5% to $55.40 after lowering its full-year guidance: It now expects to earn between $2.39 and $2.43 a share, compared with the $2.49 per-share consensus. It also received several analyst downgrades, including from Morgan Stanley, Telsey Advisory Group, and BTIG Research.
Walt Disney (DIS) is up 2.3% to $108.51 after boosting its bid for 21st Century Fox (FOXA), up 6.1% to $47.45, to $71.3 billion in cash and stock. — Teresa Rivas
Upgrades & Downgrades
Citigroup (C) is up 1.5% to $67.76 after Goldman Sachs upgraded it to Buy.
Illustration: Getty Images PTC Therapeutics (PTCT) is up 4.2% to $34.65 after Barclays upgraded it to Equal Weight.
Sally Beauty Holdings (SBH) is down 2.9% to $15.50 after Cowen & Co. downgraded it to Market Perform.
Scotts Miracle-Gro (SMG) is down 0.7% to $82 after Raymond James downgraded it to Market Perform.
Xcel Energy (XEL) is down 0.7% to $4.87 after Bank of America Merrill Lynch downgraded it to Neutral. — T.R.
